_why: Fed to Goblin Brain with `node "C:/Goblin Brain/scripts/teach.mjs" "C:/Find Aliens/docs/lessons/deep-state-and-demystification.teach.json"` from C:\xixoxis. lessons -> per-file rules Kenoma reads with the file; lore -> facts brain_lore serves; traces -> playbooks handed to later turns with a matching goal.

lore.subject: research/glm-recheck.mjs
lore.fact: Run research/glm-recheck.mjs with --strict-sources for any new page: only .gov/.mil/.edu/.int sites, recognised newsrooms, watchdogs, law firms or the subject's own site count as sources, and a fact only unrated pages state fails.

lore.subject: research/glm-recheck.mjs
lore.fact: research/glm-recheck.mjs asks Goblin Brain first (evidence.search for lines the roost already verified, sources.search for Federal Register, GovInfo, CourtListener and EDGAR records) and skips that when the Brain is down or --no-brain is passed.

lore.subject: research/glm-recheck.mjs
lore.fact: research/glm-recheck.mjs writes <out>/digest.md: rewrites that lost the original's point first, then failures, then every changed line; a person reads it before a page is built.

lore.subject: research/source-labels.mjs
lore.fact: research/source-labels.mjs (cleanPub, cleanDate, cleanSources) is the one place a source's label is shortened to a publisher and a month for Find Aliens pages.

lore.subject: public/deep-state.html
lore.fact: Deep State (public/deep-state.html, js/deep-state.js) is a pixel print of an eye in a pyramid in a stipple forest above four dossiers; its 19 facts and their quotes are in research/deep-state-sources.json.

lore.subject: public/demystification.html
lore.fact: The Demystification Desk (public/demystification.html, js/demystify.js) is a lavender pixel poster with four kanji-labelled UFO cases; its 17 verified facts and quotes are in research/demystification-sources.json.

lore.subject: research/build-deep-state.mjs
lore.fact: public/js/deep-state-data.js is generated by research/build-deep-state.mjs, which joins research/deep-state-dossiers.json (the claims) to research/deep-state-sources.json (the verified quotes) on the claim id DS-<dossier>-<item>. It exits non-zero if an id is on one side only, if the statuses disagree, if a claim cites a URL the record never opened, or if the claim's wording changed since it was checked. Run it after editing either file; --check asserts the generated file is current.

lore.subject: public/deep-state.html
lore.fact: public/deep-state.html must not link atlas-ui.css: that sheet declares --paper as a dark panel colour (var(--paper, #161813)) while this page's --paper is the print's paper white, so every .atlas-* class would resolve its background to white. Write the handful of pill and stamp rules into the page instead.

lore.subject: public/js/deep-state.js
lore.fact: THE CUT's SURFACE constant in public/js/deep-state.js and `.cut-bands { top }` in public/deep-state.html are the same fraction in two files; the four band links are real HTML laid over the canvas, because deep-state.js carries no bitmap font (blind-pool.js is the file that does). The buried pyramid takes its half-width from its own height so it stays steep at any canvas size, and the trench is drawn before the pyramid so the apex it exposes is not whited out.

lore.subject: research/extract-entities.mjs
lore.fact: research/extract-entities.mjs is broken as of October 2026: pageData() evaluates each page's last inline script in a bare vm context and public/blind-pool.html throws 'window is not defined', which blocks regenerating public/data/entities.json for every page. Unrelated to the Deep State rebuild.

lore.subject: public/img
lore.fact: Open Graph cards for the Gazette's canvas pages are composed in the page itself - the live canvas drawn into a 1200x630 buffer at an exact integer scale with the title typeset under it - not screenshotted, because a screenshot is resampled by the device pixel ratio and breaks the pixel grid. Quantise to 64 colours before saving.

lore.subject: research/glm-recheck.mjs
lore.fact: The mechanical checks in research/glm-recheck.mjs cannot catch a rewrite that keeps the draft's framing and swaps the subject: building deep-state dossier 05 it wrote that Glenn Greenwald 'argued that ... intelligence tradecraft becomes once it is available for hire', a sentence he never said, and it passed because there was no figure or name to fail on. Read every rewrite against its quotes and restate on the subject's own words, marking the line `edited`.

lore.subject: public/deep-state.html
lore.fact: Quotes on public/deep-state.html get typographic marks from .quote::before/::after, so a quote that already carries the source's own quotation marks is tagged .quote.bare and the pseudo-elements are suppressed. A check for doubled marks must not be written against textContent, which excludes pseudo-element content and reports clean however broken the page looks.

lore.subject: public/js/deep-state.js
lore.fact: THE CUT's band count is not written down twice: .cut-bands takes --cut-layers from DOSSIERS.length and public/js/deep-state.js reads .cut-band back off the DOM into LAYERS. Canvas height is 0.1 x LAYERS of its width (0.195 on a phone) so a band stays ~52px at 375px, and the pyramid's apex is a fraction of the ground's depth rather than a count of bands. A new dossier still needs a glyph that exists in GLYPHS.

traces.prompt: Re-research a Find Aliens investigation page and rebuild it from verified facts only (no Wikipedia, every claim checked against its source)

steps.result: list every factual claim the page makes; phrase each the way a source would state it, with a status (law, documented, reported, words, argument)
facts as [{id, status, text}]; hints map an id to primary-source URLs (Federal Register, the agency's page, the court opinion, the company's release)
GLM-5.3-flash reads pages; a quote counts only if it is on the fetched page; figures must be in a quote in the same unit; names on a cited page; rated sources only. About $0.04 for 19 facts.
read the LOST rewrites first, then the failures, then every change; a source's own typo and a stale figure pass every mechanical check
with better hints: the primary record, or the Internet Archive copy of an old government URL (2015 and 2010 captures)
accept near-misses only with a why (a sum of receipts, a number spelled out, a name written in full); reword only to what the quotes state
the page is built from verified facts only; unconfirmed lines are left out, and research/<page>-sources.json keeps every quote
judge the page from full-size screenshots and fix overlaps at phone width before committing
